title: traffic-thermostat-probabilistic-slo-controller-with-confidence-decay
creator: Aisha Rivera
description: Build a probabilistic SLO-based rollback controller ("traffic thermostat") that automatically adjusts traffic during model rollouts using calibrated confidence bands and a time-decayed posterior to avoid noisy flip-flops. The controller considers latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput signals across cohorts and exposes tuning knobs for teams and automatic suggestions from Optimize.
problem_statement: Current canary rollouts use fixed thresholds and simple rule-based aborts which cause oscillation under bursty traffic and produce false positives when SLO signals are sparse (low traffic cohorts). We need an automated mechanism that is robust to low-sample cohorts, combines heterogeneous signals, and provides human-understandable rationales for rollback decisions.
proposed_solution: Implement a controller that computes a Bayesian posterior over the delta between baseline and candidate model SLOs for each metric (latency p95, error rate, token cost per 1k tokens, throughput). Use an exponential time-decay on observations to prioritize recent behavior. Convert posteriors into a calibrated "comfort band" with programmable strictness per metric. Generate a composite risk score via weighted pooling (weights configurable per project) and translate risk to traffic actions (hold, slow-roll, rollback). The controller will also export explainability artifacts (cohort-level deltas, posterior samples, and feature contributions) to the Console for audits and postmortems.
design_notes: Signal model: treat latency as log-normal for posterior computation, error rate as beta-binomial, token cost as Gaussian on normalized cost-per-token, throughput as Poisson arrival model for volume-aware adjustments.
Confidence decay: exponential half-life configurable (default 30 minutes) to avoid stale observations leading to incorrect rollbacks after traffic pattern shifts.
Cohorting: evaluate signals per-route, per-region, and per-customer-tier; aggregate with hierarchical pooling to borrow strength when cohort samples are low.
Fallback logic: when model variants are incompatible, automatically shift to nearest-compatible variant (quantized/FP16 fallback) before full rollback.
UI hooks: add new rollout timeline visualization with posterior bands and suggested action and allow operator override with reason required for manual rollback.
Privacy: metrics used are aggregated; raw requests never leave customer control plane for Private deployments. Audit logs will record decision inputs and outputs.
Config: expose metric weights, confidence thresholds, decay half-life, and minimum sample sizes as part of rollout policy schema.
Observability: record posterior mean, 95% credible interval, composite risk score, and decision reason in trace/span tags for correlating with traces.
Performance budget: controller inference must add <5ms median latency to routing path; heavy posterior recomputation should run async and not block traffic shift decisions when possible.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype - implement Bayesian posteriors and single-metric controller in a feature branch; unit tests for statistical conversions (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Cohort pooling and decay - add hierarchical pooling and configurable decay; integrate with metric ingestion pipeline and Console visualization (3 weeks).
Phase 3: Composite risk and policy schema - implement weighted pooling, traffic action translation, and policy API; add UI controls in rollouts page (3 weeks).
Phase 4: Canary trials - run internal canaries on dev clusters and 3 customer staging rollouts; collect telemetry and tune default weights (2 weeks).
Phase 5: Hardening & docs - resilience tests, chaos-simulated burst traffic, runbook, and public docs/SDK examples (2 weeks).
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes per-metric posteriors and exposes mean and 95% credible interval for p95 latency, error rate, token cost delta, and throughput deviation.
In 10 synthetic burst scenarios controller avoids >50% unnecessary rollbacks compared to baseline rule-based guardrails while still catching regressions with magnitude >=20% on a majority of trials.
Traffic adjustment actions (hold/slow-roll/rollback) are executed within 30s of policy decision and recorded in rollout timeline and audit logs.
Default policy and decay settings demonstrated to be stable across three customer staging rollouts with differing traffic distributions.
Acceptance tests and chaos scenarios are automated and pass in CI; PRs include integration tests for decision reproducibility.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Bayesian model mis-specification could under- or over-estimate risk for heavy-tailed latency distributions. Mitigation: use log transforms and empirical checks; add a fallback threshold if posterior variance is extreme.

Risk: Low-sample cohorts may be dominated by priors leading to missed regressions. Mitigation: hierarchical pooling and minimum-sample gating before auto-rollback; surface low-sample warnings in Console.

Risk: Operators may distrust automated decisions. Mitigation: provide explainability artifacts and require justification for manual overrides; rollout an "audit-mode" where actions are suggested but not executed for initial customers.
Risk: Performance cost of posterior recomputation at high route cardinality. Mitigation: async recompute with cached decisions and incremental updates; cap recompute frequency with TTL per cohort.

comments: 2026-02-15 Aisha Rivera: Initial triage and problem framing. Ran offline sims with existing canary rules; observed oscillation under spiky arrivals. Decided to pursue posterior-based approach to quantify uncertainty.

2026-02-22 Ravi Patel: Prototype for latency and error-rate posteriors committed. Implemented log-normal transform for latency. PR opened: runtime/pull/3847. Benchmarked compute cost — median extra CPU per route ~2ms when cached.

2026-02-28 Design review (Maya Thompson): Requested clearer UI affordance for manual overrides and required a justification field for audits. Also suggested adding a minimum sample-size gating in policy.

2026-03-04 QA note (Diego Morales): Added chaos test scenarios to simulate region failover; observed that decay half-life needed to be reduced to recover faster after failovers. Adjusting default to 15 minutes for region failover-sensitive routes.
2026-03-09 PM feedback (Sofia Nguyen): Ask to expose default weight presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and ensure Optimize can suggest presets based on historical cost/latency tradeoffs.

2026-03-12 Ravi Patel: Ran three internal staging canaries; controller detected a synthetic token-cost regression early and executed a slow-roll action which prevented widespread degradation. Collected telemetry; next step is to add hierarchical pooling tuning and finalize policy schema.
